second_order: building and guarding Polish pictures together
theme_note: These codes all contribute to making a shared Polish picture persist: calling people in, agreeing coordinates or templates, placing and repairing pixels, warning of overwriting, redirecting effort, and limiting work to conservation. What varies is the picture (flag, Polandball, Pope), whether the turn plans or performs work, and whether guarding means repair, restraint, or redirecting an attack.

second_order: working out how to share the canvas with neighbours
theme_note: These codes negotiate coexistence at the edge of the flag: asking that work be spared, offering alliance, reporting that named neighbours got along, and admitting expansion violated stated restraint. What varies is who approaches whom and whether the turn offers peace, reports accommodation, or exposes its failure.

second_order: running and disputing the subreddit’s own April Fools jokes
theme_note: These codes use or contest changes in the subreddit itself rather than the canvas: missing voting arrows, imposed Stonoga styling, a quotation game, and a disguised Rickroll. What varies is whether participants investigate the joke, perform it, challenge moderator authority, or spring a one-post trick.
This code publicly claims a shared result in the room’s own words; later slices can show whether celebration also becomes mourning or retrospective credit-giving.
This attack call belongs with no other slice-01 practice: the reply that redirects it is work of guarding the Polish flag and is grouped there.

second_order: moving plans into Discord, megathreads, scripts and bots
theme_note: These codes organise how pixel work and talk will be coordinated: sending people to Discord or pinned plans, asking for one thread, and recommending scripts or bots. What varies is whether coordination moves venue, contains subreddit traffic, or automates placement.

second_order: arguing over what the pixel project means
theme_note: These codes evaluate the project rather than merely naming a target: calling it nationalist competition, amplifying that provocation, questioning attacks on a harmless rainbow, defending the chance to do something together, and disputing whether recolouring destroys or plays with the rainbow. What varies is the moral vocabulary and whether the speaker condemns, defends, or reinterprets the work.

second_order: recounting and mourning what happened on the canvas
theme_note: These codes turn ongoing or completed pixel work into a story or commemoration: recounting the start, staging a battle reconstruction, crediting reinforcements, mourning a swallowed logo, and recalling mutual help. What varies is whether the account is comic history, credit-giving, mourning, or coalition memory.

second_order: calling to overwrite other people’s pictures
theme_note: These codes propose expansion or deliberate alteration of other work: a reverse Anschluss, eating Soylent, adding a swastika, and placing a large EU flag over the UK. What varies is the target and whether the proposed overwrite is framed as conquest, humour, or replacement.

second_order: denying that organised Poles control every Polish pixel
theme_note: These codes draw a boundary between coordinated participants and uncontrolled placers: accepting a deal without speaking for everyone, separating Discord restraint from outsiders, allowing expansion may be spontaneous, and calling an attack a false flag. What varies is whether the limit qualifies a promise, explains damage, or refuses blame.

second_order: showing an r/place image and asking what the room thinks
theme_note: This single code is an open request for the room’s response to an image and belongs with no other practice in the slice.

second_order: listing, policing and testing people who change the eagle
theme_note: These codes act on contested edits to the Polish eagle by proposing a name list, invoking the anti-witch-hunt rule, repurposing the list as a troll database, and testing how quickly deliberate damage is repaired. What varies is whether participants seek deterrence, impose a platform limit, recruit provocateurs, or probe the repair response.

second_order: trying to start another shared action after r/place
theme_note: These codes negotiate whether the room should begin a themed meme day after the canvas: one proposes it, another says r/place already filled the front page, and another says people are resting. What varies is the call, the saturation objection, and the explanation for non-participation.
